tools.usecase: See the matching rule for each supplied URL before you change robots.txt. Nothing is fetched or submitted.

inputs.label: robots.txt content
inputs.help: Paste the file content or choose a UTF-8 .txt file. Maximum 64 KiB. Google-style Allow/Disallow matching; unsupported directives are reported.

inputs.label: URLs to test
inputs.help: One absolute HTTP(S) URL per line, from one origin: the same scheme, host and port. Up to 5,000 URLs. The URLs are never visited.

boundaries: Tests supplied rules only; live robots.txt, HTTP status, page meta directives and indexing remain unknown.
Allowing crawling does not guarantee indexing. A robots.txt block is not a noindex instruction.
Supports Google-style group selection, Allow/Disallow, * and terminal $. Crawl-delay, Host, Noindex and unknown directives are displayed but not applied.

inputs.label: Redirect mappings CSV
inputs.help: Required headers: from,to. Optional: status. Absolute HTTP(S) URLs only. Up to 5,000 mappings. Missing status stays unknown.

boundaries: This checks a supplied plan, not live redirects or response headers. Final targets are terminal entries in the map, not verified 200 pages.
URL identity is exact after surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Case, query and trailing slash are preserved.

Language-tag shape is checked, not every ISO language/region assignment or Google support. Conflicting language slots are excluded from self-reference and return-link inference.

tools.usecase: Bring your crawl signals and optional sitemap or Search Console observations. See where the supplied evidence agrees, conflicts or leaves a question open.

inputs.label: Crawl signals CSV
inputs.help: Required: url and at least one of status,robots,canonical. HTTP status must be a numeric code from 100 to 599. Up to 5,000 rows.

inputs.label: Sitemap URLs (optional)
inputs.help: One absolute HTTP(S) URL per line, a CSV with url or loc, or an XML urlset. Up to 5,000 URLs. Omit this input to keep sitemap membership unknown.

boundaries: Reports observations in supplied files only. Aligned supplied signals do not establish live indexability, Google indexing, rankings or an outcome.

Missing, invalid and conflicting observations remain distinct. Canonical targets outside the crawl or in conflicting crawl rows stay unknown. All applicable findings are exported; the primary label is only a review order.

URL joins preserve the exact trimmed string, including case, query and trailing slash. Robots none means noindex and nofollow. Unrecognized directives cannot prove an index signal. Crawler-scoped directives are preserved as text but their applicability remains unknown.
Search Console status and dates are supplied text, not API verification. No native coverage export layout is assumed. Missing sitemap or Search Console input stays unknown.

tools.name: Redirect Rule Compiler
tools.title: Free Cloudflare Static _redirects Draft from CSV | Base2026
tools.description: Turn a CSV map into a draft Cloudflare static assets _redirects file. Exclude conflicting paths, cycles and unsafe syntax. Local processing; test the draft in staging.

og.title: Free Cloudflare Static _redirects Draft from CSV | Base2026
og.description: Turn a CSV map into a draft Cloudflare static assets _redirects file. Exclude conflicting paths, cycles and unsafe syntax. Local processing; test the draft in staging.

tools.usecase: Turn your supplied map into an exact-path _redirects draft for Cloudflare static assets. Review excluded rows, then test the draft in staging before use.

inputs.label: Redirect mappings CSV
inputs.help: Required headers: from,to. Optional: status. Use exact root-relative paths or HTTP(S) source URLs from one origin. Up to 2,000 mappings. Queries in either source or target are excluded.

boundaries: Emits a draft for exact paths in Cloudflare static assets _redirects only. It does not generate Workers routing, Bulk Redirects, Apache, NGINX or Vercel configuration. Test host routing, asset and Worker precedence, incoming-query behavior and redirects in staging. No server behavior is verified here.

Queries in either source or target are excluded: this MVP does not choose query preservation or replacement behavior. Incoming request queries still require staging checks. Fragments, dot segments, protocol-relative URLs, whitespace, controls, wildcards, placeholders and ambiguous escapes are excluded.

Absolute source URLs must have one origin. Mixed origins quarantine the entire batch; no first-row origin wins. With one origin, the draft paths apply to the deployment host, which you must verify. Paths keep exact case, slash and percent-escape spelling.

Cycles, conflicting sources and paths reaching excluded mappings are withheld. Chain flattening is off by default; opting in permits only identical status codes. Terminal targets are supplied map endpoints, not verified live destinations.

Local safety caps: 2,000 input rows, 4,096 characters per URL and 1,000 characters per emitted line. ASCII paths or unambiguous percent-encoded UTF-8 only. These bounds do not establish compatibility with your deployment.

inputs.label: Inlinks CSV

inputs.label: URL inventory CSV (optional)

URLs keep exact identity after surrounding whitespace trimming, including case, trailing slash and query. Fragments, credentials, invalid URLs and links whose source or target is outside the selected origin are excluded and reported.
Exact duplicate input rows remain link occurrences and are flagged. Inventory conflicts stay UNKNOWN; no first row wins. Known followed, known nofollow and unknown-follow counts stay separate.

Anchors are grouped by Unicode NFC, lowercase and collapsed whitespace. Shared text across targets is SHARED_ANCHOR_TARGETS_REVIEW, not cannibalization. Generic examples are click here, read more, learn more, here and read the related guide; context may make them useful.

og.title: Free GSC Period Change Analyzer from CSV Exports | Base2026
og.description: Compare GSC CSV exports by page, query or prepared key. Calculate observed click, impression, CTR and position changes locally while preserving missing and invalid evidence.

tools.usecase: Compare two exported periods without uploading client data. Review the largest observed changes, keep missing rows unknown and use a descriptive click decomposition when both periods have impressions.

inputs.label: Before period CSV
inputs.help: English headers only: Page / Top pages / URL, Query / Top queries, or Key; plus Clicks and Impressions. Optional CTR and Position / Average position. Counts are ungrouped nonnegative integers.

inputs.label: After period CSV
inputs.help: Use the same key type and comparable period length, search type and filters. These conditions cannot be verified from the CSV. Missing rows are UNKNOWN, never zero.

boundaries: Describes supplied exported rows only. Period length, search type, filters and property comparability are NOT VERIFIED. GSC exports can be limited to top rows; anonymized queries and omitted rows prevent treating the export as complete property totals.

Missing rows, blank metrics, invalid metrics and conflicting duplicate keys stay distinct. Exact identical rows may collapse with notice; conflicting rows are quarantined. Positions are never aggregated across duplicates.

CTR is clicks / impressions when impressions are positive. With zero impressions, CTR and decomposition are UNKNOWN. Percentage change from a zero baseline is undefined, not Infinity. Lower position numbers are better; the reported position delta is after minus before.
No algorithm penalty, technical cause, ranking explanation or guaranteed opportunity is inferred. Findings identify observed deltas and evidence needing review, without a confidence or SEO score.

og.description: Audit a metadata CSV for missing or duplicate titles and descriptions. Preview supplied text, review social fields and download the results. Free, local processing.

tools.usecase: Review the metadata in your export. Find missing or repeated titles and descriptions, then select a row to see an illustrative text preview.

inputs.label: Page metadata CSV
inputs.help: Required: url,title,description. Optional: h1,og_title,og_description,og_image,twitter_card. Explicit crawler aliases are supported; duplicate or ambiguous headers are rejected.

boundaries: Blank CSV records are ignored. Counts and exports cover the rows checked. Result rows are numbered sequentially and are not line numbers in your input file. No skipped-record count is inferred.
Audits supplied CSV observations only. Missing columns are UNKNOWN; a supplied blank cell is MISSING. No live tags, URLs, image files, indexing or search results are verified.

Character counts use Unicode code points after NFC normalization, whitespace collapse and trimming. They are not grapheme counts, pixel measurements, length recommendations or Google truncation limits.

Duplicate titles/descriptions mean identical case-sensitive normalized text across distinct valid supplied URL strings. Repeated rows for one URL are reported separately; invalid URL rows stay visible but do not enter cross-URL duplicate groups.

Title/H1 equality or difference is informational. It does not predict a Google title rewrite, quality, rankings or CTR. Social states inventory supplied text only; SUPPLIED does not validate tag syntax, image availability, dimensions or a rendered card.
The selectable preview formats your supplied text illustratively. Google may choose different title or snippet text. It is not a live SERP or a device-specific simulation.
CSV exports quote cells and prefix common spreadsheet formula-leading values with an apostrophe. Review imported spreadsheet behavior; exported copies are files you choose to retain.

tools.name: JSON-LD Graph Inspector
tools.title: Free JSON-LD Graph Inspector & Syntax Validator | Base2026
tools.description: Inspect a JSON-LD graph locally: check JSON syntax, inventory nested entities and review exact @id references. No URL fetching or rich-result eligibility claims.

og.title: Free JSON-LD Graph Inspector & Syntax Validator | Base2026
og.description: Inspect a JSON-LD graph locally: check JSON syntax, inventory nested entities and review exact @id references. No URL fetching or rich-result eligibility claims.

tools.usecase: Paste raw JSON-LD to inspect its objects, types and @id references. Keep parsing, entity inventory and reference coverage separate while you review the supplied graph.

inputs.label: Raw JSON-LD
inputs.help: Paste one JSON object or array, or choose a UTF-8 .json or .jsonld file. Exclude HTML and script tags. Maximum 2 MiB; no URL or remote context is requested.

boundaries: Inspect raw JSON-LD only. HTML extraction, URL requests, remote contexts, JSON-LD expansion and Schema.org vocabulary validation are not performed.

Parsing, entity inventory and reference coverage are separate observations. Parsed JSON or matching references do not establish fully valid JSON-LD, Google rich-result eligibility, visible-page agreement, rankings or traffic effects.

Objects in root arrays, @graph and nested properties are inspected. Empty objects, pure @graph/@context containers and @value/@list/@set wrappers are not entity rows; their nested objects are still inspected. Objects inside @context are counted for limits but are not entities.

Only literal keywords are recognized. Contexts and aliases are not expanded or applied, and types are supplied labels rather than verified vocabulary terms. A missing context or type is not automatically an invalid graph.

An @id-only reference has exactly one member, @id, with a string value. A definition has a string @id and another member besides @id or @context. Exact supplied strings match without trimming, URL normalization or base resolution; reference strings are not followed.

An unmatched reference with a URI scheme has external-definition state UNKNOWN. Other unmatched strings, including fragments, relative paths, blank-node labels and the empty string, are local references not matched in this input. Neither observation proves that the published graph is broken.

Several definition objects can share an @id. They are retained as multiple definitions for review; fragments are not inherently invalid. Merging, equivalence and conflicting-property semantics are not implemented.
Native JSON.parse keeps the last value of repeated member names within one object; these duplicate member names are not separately diagnosed. Separate objects with the same @id are retained.

Limits apply before a complete result is returned: 2 MiB UTF-8, 5,000 objects including contexts, 20,000 total values, 64 nested object/array levels, 16,384 UTF-16 units per string/member name and 4,096 per JSON pointer. Reduce or split the input if a limit is reached; partial inventories are not exported.
CSV copies use the unchanged shared quoting and formula-prefix protection. Input and results stay in tab memory until cleared, navigation or closing; downloads are files you choose to keep.
